text:
alerts-bot: ALERT: p99 TLS handshake latency spike in eu-west for route /v1/completions - +420ms over baseline. Incident link: https://console.redwood/company/incidents/INC-2026-042
emma: Customer FinTechX raised a support ticket. They see 600-900ms p99 on requests from DE; customer shows series of failed handshakes and 504s. Raised to us. Ticket #FTX-1284
emma: repro steps from customer: run curl from eu-central VM -> api.redwood.example and measure time_appconnect
emma: pasted sample: 
```
$ curl -w "%{time_connect} %{time_appconnect}" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.example
0.064 0.558
```
jordan: @emma got it. Can someone grab recent egress traceroutes and edge logs for the EU POPs? Suspect cross-zone hop increase or BGP change. Also any GSLB rollout in last 24h?
jordan: quick check: run `mtr -c 100 -r -w api.redwood.eu-west` from probe pool and paste headers
diego: I'm seeing similar small bumps in metrics 00:42-01:10 UTC on eu-west-pop3. TLS handshakes p99 up ~450ms. No config rollouts on our side. Possibly upstream peering flaps.
sam-k: For mitigation, enable fallback to eu-west-pop1 for affected customers and add a temporary policy to prefer lower handshake latency routes. I can push route override, need green from oncall.
emma: Done. I pushed canary override to route policy id rp-843 and enabled 15m TTL. Monitoring now.
diego: Also enabling handshake short-circuiting on the edge runtime for cached client certs for FinTechX API key to avoid renegotiation penalty.
emma: Running capture: 
```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (10.2.3.4), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
1 10.1.0.1 0.2 ms 0.3 ms 0.3 ms
2 192.0.2.1 1.1 ms 1.1 ms 1.2 ms
3 203.0.113.1 45.0 ms 46.2 ms 47.1 ms
4 198.51.100.1 410.0 ms 412.3 ms 415.6 ms
```
jordan: That hop at 4 looks like cross-region hairpin or peering issue. Filing with core-net: ticket CN-5621. Linking traceroutes and pcap.
emma: customer confirmed initial improvement after override, p99 dropped to ~160ms. Will keep oncall monitoring and update the support ticket.
diego: Plan: core-net to investigate peering flaps; ops to keep override for 30m and then rollback if stable; if not stable, escalate to peering provider. Assigning @jordan to own rollback and CN coordination.
jordan: ack. I'll follow up in CN ticket and ping here when core-net responds. :thumbsup:
